project.title: Fungal taxa transported by long-distance migratory birds to the boreal north
project.description: Long-distance dispersal influences the abundance and distribution of organisms on large geographical scales, and has profound consequences for populations, communities, ecosystems and human societies. Fungal dispersal is typically thought to occur mainly via aerial transport of dispersal propagules. There is increasing evidence that alternative dispersal mechanisms, such as animal-mediated dispersal, can be important in fungal ecology and potentially contribute to dispersal events even across long distances. However, examples of animals transporting fungal material across long distances are rare. To identify these long-distance transport events, we characterise fungal assemblages attached to feathers and feet of long-distance migratory passerines arriving in southern Finland in the spring migration season, using environmental DNA metabarcoding. We detected over 450 fungal taxa attached to birds, with marked differences in assemblage composition between spring and autumn migratory seasons and between bird species. Notable detected taxa include many plant pathogenic fungi, especially Podosphaeria leucotricha and Monilinia spp., economically important pathogens of apple trees. No fungal taxa clearly originating from bird overwintering areas in the tropics were detected. Our results suggest that many of the detected fungal taxa originate at least from across the Gulf of Finland, nearly 100 km south from the bird sampling location. We discuss the implications of bird-mediated long-distance fungal transport, especially in the context of detected plant pathogens.
project.center_name: Finnish Museum of Natural History / University of Helsinki
